We've been warning people not to share sensitive personal information with AI chatbots, because most companies use the conversations as training data — but now there's an even bigger reason to be careful.

Things went from bad to worse over the weekend, when Reddit users discovered that some Claude AI chat logs could be accessed via a simple Google search……

Claude chats leaked

Claude has a share function, which lets you share chat conversations with colleagues, friends, or family members. The chatbot generates a link that you can send to one or more people, and Claude implicitly assures you that nobody who knows that URL will be able to view the conversation.

The problem, as Reddit users discovered, is that you didn't actually need the link to view the conversation. You just needed to search Google, either using specific search terms, or simply asking Google to show all conversations shared in this way. As BBC News reported:

All you have to do is ask Google to search the directory used for sharing Claude conversations (site:claude.ai/share), and you can see them all.

As you'd expect, some of the chat conversations were absolutely ridiculous, such as someone asking why the music industry was covering up the fact that most of Jay-Z's albums were co-written by birds. But others contained extremely sensitive information, such as text logs of private conversations; a lawyer asking whether they needed to self-report misconduct; and a user who inadvertently leaked their own private keys while asking for help setting up a crypto wallet.

Anthropic is still trying to claim that this is not a problem.

Reality, of course, is that this is absolutely a serious problem, because it's completely outside what users would expect. Worse still, Wired reported that the underlying cause appears to have been an egregious case of professional negligence.

This comes the day after news reports that Claude Cowork was able to escape its sandbox on a Mac, gaining full access to all files.

How to protect yourself

The problem appears to have been at least partially addressed, with previously searchable results now returning errors, but given that the share feature relies on "security through obscurity," I would still recommend avoiding using it.

I would also recommend deleting any conversations you've previously shared. You can do this in Settings > Privacy > Shared Conversations > Manage.

Once again proving Apple was right all along

Apple Intelligence and the new Siri take a three-tier approach to privacy:

  • Where possible, AI processing is done on-device
  • The first fallback is to use Apple's own Private Cloud Compute (PCC) servers
  • Only then is a Gemini model used, with the same level of PCC protections

The elaborate PCC architecture means that absolutely no data can be accessed by Apple or Google, and nothing is retained. The security architecture Apple has designed allows independent security researchers to verify it.

  • Official Apple Store on Amazon
  • Discounted AirPods Pro 3

  • AirTag cases and accessories
